<description>
`m_last_good` is used to prevent recording failed attempts for addresses when it is our connectivity that is at fault.
However, it is quite common that only some networks are unreachable - e.g. I have encountered it frequently that `IPv6` is unreachable, while `IPv4` works fine. In this case it is not correct to increase the failed counter for an `IPv6` address  and ultimately making it `Terrible`, just because we are making `IPv4` connections.

Fix this by making `m_last_good` network-specific.
Also change the initial value from 1 to 0, so that in a situation when there was no previous attempt for an address, but also no previous successful connection to its network, the failed count is not increased. The intial value was not a major issue previously because we would [only count failures](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/18c05d93016b28a9afd4c716dfe00b6e0accb30b/src/net.cpp#L2935-L2939) after having at least two outbound connections (in which case `m_last_good` would have been set).
</description>

have you also considered cloud node operators? there are many of them and I think they often don't have ipv6 enabled. but they receive ipv6 gossip and store in their addrman. not sure how many would change bitcoin.conf to specify `-onlynet=ipv4`.

so not fully comfortable with the idea of them getting squatter ipv6 addresses in their new table which would slowly grow over time. for these cloud nodes, an ipv6 entry could then take a terrible ipv4 slot but never give it back (under normal self announcement gossip scenario), so i'd expect the ipv6 share to creep up rather than stay where it is?

just for reference - some stats from different peer.observer addrman snapshots on master which don't support ipv6:
- seeing 3.8k - 15.8k slots in the new table occupied by ipv6 addresses (out of 64k slots)
    - for the 3.8k ipv6 in new table : 605 (`nAttempts=0`) + 1,122 (`nAttempts=1`) + 2,045 (`nAttempts=2`) + 67 ( (`nAttempts>=3`)
    - for the 15.8k ipv6 in new table: 3,285 (`nAttempts=0`) + 4,713 (`nAttempts=1`) + 7,547 (`nAttempts=2`) +  22 (`nAttempts>=3`)
- currently IPv6 gossip is 25.9–27.6% of IPv4+IPv6 gossip per day. this could change over the years.

makes sense. wondering if it's worth it to find a possible middle-ground between:
- stopping a temporary network outage on our side from marking good addresses `isTerrible` (marking all ipv6 as `isTerrible` and everything getting evicted)
- on a node that doesn't support ipv6 - stopping ipv6 addresses from holding new-table slots indefinitely (marking no ipv6 as `isTerrible` and nothing getting evicted)

maybe If we haven't connected to ipv6 for 7 days while other networks work, an ipv4 gossip received can take the new table slot of an address on the broken connectivity network?
